messages:
alex: Hey all — p95 for hosted text-gen spiked to ~4.2s at 11:02 UTC, p99 ~6.5s. Alert fired for api-prod-route-21. Queue depth jumped briefly to ~80-90. I'm starting a quick triage.
priya: Noted. We rolled the kselector heuristic v2 to canary at ~10:50 for better batching affinity. 50% canary per deploy-bot. Could be related.
sam: I pulled a flameprofile from the canary node. Kernel selection path is showing a 140–260ms tail on select_kernel() when seq_len > 800. That adds up at p95. Also saw increased GPU busy stalls while waiting for batch assembly.
luis: KV cache graphs: prefix hit rate dropped from 92% -> 68% around the same time, eviction rate x2. Tenant-42 has multiple long context requests, looks like hot prefixes causing thrash.
jamie: quick logs snippet from one affected host: ```[11:02:57.123] route=api-prod-route-21 qdepth=88 batch_ready=0 kselector_ms=248 kv_miss=1 batch_size=1```
priya: Hmm — v2 kselector prioritizes kernel affinity over merging short sequences; seems to avoid padding larger sequences into smaller-kernel batches which increased batch churn for mixed-len traffic.
alex: So combination: kselector-v2 + noisy long-context tenant -> smaller useful batching + more kselector decisions -> higher per-request overhead.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout metrics: success_rate 99.98%, latency_increase_detected=true flagged at 11:03.
jamie: I also profiled the scheduler: coalesce_timeout stayed at 12ms but effective wait time dropped because selector rejected a lot of coalescing opportunities. Many requests fell through to single-request kernels.
sam: Attached quick perf counters (summarized): ``kselector_calls: +35%``, ``avg_kernel_select_ms: 0.18 -> 0.34``, ``coalesce_hits: -47%``, ``avg_batch_size: 4.8 -> 2.1``.
luis: Tenant throttling idea: we could apply a short soft-rate cap to tenant-42 to reduce prefix churn while we revert. Thoughts?
priya: Agreed — rollback kselector-v2 on hosted canary ASAP to confirm. If rollback brings p95 down, we can iterate on v2. Also start a temporary per-tenant dampening rule for tenants with >N concurrent long-context streams.
alex: I'll run rollback. Can someone confirm canary routing is still at 50%?
deploy-bot: Rolling back kselector-v2 on canary pool now -> started. Estimated completion in ~45s.
jamie: After 90s: observed p95 drop from 4200ms -> 950ms on canary nodes. Queue depth back under 20. Coalesce hits rising.
sam: Great. That strongly implicates the selector heuristic. We should still address KV thrash — cache prefetch/pinning for hot prefixes could help.
luis: I've enabled a soft-limit on tenant-42 (concurrency limit = 6) for 10m as a safety net. Monitoring.
priya: Action items: 1) revert canary = done (alex/deploy-bot), 2) throttle noisy tenant (luis), 3) run a controlled perf test of kselector-v2 with pinned-prefetch enabled (sam/jamie), 4) postmortem + perf regression ticket (priya).
alex: Thanks. Can we capture profiler trace and dump a minimal repro? Sam/jamie, pair to produce perf trace and a short script that generates mixed-length traffic to reproduce. Put artifacts in #perf-artifacts.
sam: On it. I'll run nsight + our trace sampler and strip to a 30s sample.
jamie: I'll write a small harness that replays a 70/30 mix of long/short chats, sequence lengths 64/1200, 200 RPS, with fingerprinted tenant id to emulate tenant-42 pattern.
luis: Monitoring shows p95 continuing to normalize after rollback and throttle. I'll keep the throttle for 10m and then relax if stable.
priya: Filing regression ticket: PERF-8342 — include traces, coalesce metrics, kselector diff, KV cache stats. We'll schedule a dedicated session to redesign v2 to account for mixed-len workloads and add a safety check to not reduce coalescing below a threshold.
alex: Good work. Keep updates here. We'll follow up with a short postmortem once we have artifacts. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Incident resolved on canary pool. Follow-up: create postmortem in 24h.
deploy-bot: Note: deploys will block kselector-v2 until regression signoff.
priya: Closing triage — moving to postmortem queue.
